reviewed_finding: The DAG node is a DEFINITION: <> is a literal inscription, supplied or mentioned, with no object-language meaning until a separate admission event; it is NOT defined as Real_0 = Difference + Structure, and MSS-0 admits only <>. The Lean source GenesisConstruction.lean states the supply-inertness as an explicit hypothesis, not a theorem, and says it derives no incidence from the spelling of <>; the Rust construction requires the first event to be Supply("<>") and its admission step returns the state unchanged on Supply. The DAG-local Lean theorem pg_root_coproduct_inert_diamond_and_six_operation_separation and the Rust tranche-11 witness are vacuous fixed arithmetic about numerals and a hard-coded vector (they never mention <> or admission). A definition has no proof obligation; this node therefore builds a three-event finite model of the Rust/Lean admission fragment and proves its consistency (inertness for every function of the outcome) and independence from the coproduct identification, with the inertness shown to be the model rule rather than a consequence of the spelling.

claim_boundary.supports: The node is a DEFINITION, so the result is a consistency and independence result for it, not a proof of it. In a three-event finite admission model (supply, admit datum, admit form) in which supply is STIPULATED to be the identity on the admitted state, the kernel proves (lean4/InertDiamond.lean, over any token type with decidable equality): in the UNROOTED replay, deleting every supply event changes no outcome or refusal, so any function of the outcome is independent of how many times, or where, <> (or any token) is mentioned; in the ROOTED replay (the model of the Rust gate: the first event must be the supply of <>) the FIRST supply is an admission precondition (omitting it from an accepted history is refused) and every later supply is inert; only admission-class events can change the state, and admitting a not-yet-admitted token does; a history that only supplies and admits <> never satisfies the model predicate HasCoproduct (an admitted Difference-classified datum and an admitted Structure-classified datum) for ANY classification of tokens (Lean statement; the native replay uses one fixed classification); the predicate HasCoproduct is independent of inscribing <> (same supply subsequence, one history without and one with two admitted channel data); the identification Real_0 = Difference join Structure is NOT modelled; "coproduct predicate without any supply of <>" is realised only in the UNROOTED model (the rooted replay refuses it for lacking the root event), so in the rooted model inscription is necessary and only its non-sufficiency is shown; and inertness is a rule of the step function, not of the spelling: a rival rule under which supply admits is exhibited. Exhaustive native replay of all 8-event traces of length <= 5 (37449 traces), with a rooted-replay column set (later supplies change the rooted outcome in 0 traces; omitting the root supply is refused for 1, 7, 49, 343, 2401 histories at lengths 1 to 5; the rooted gate refuses 7, 49, ... histories the unrooted model accepts). The zero native counts of supply-deletion and prefix-mention differences follow from supply being the identity by definition and corroborate the implementation, not the inertness hypothesis. The correspondence of the model rules (supply is the identity, arity 0 refused, re-admission designates) to the Rust admission step rests on reading omega_ooutwire_primitives/src/admission.rs, which is not among the run inputs; the gate on the first event is read from genesis_construction.rs line 174.
claim_boundary.does_not_support: The identification Real_0 = Difference joined with Structure (it is not modelled; only a stand-in predicate is shown independent of the inscription); the remaining three events of the six-operation alphabet (instance, rule, imposition) and their refusal rules; the Rust partial admission rules beyond the three-event fragment; any claim that supply is inert independently of the stipulated step rule; inertness of the FIRST supply in the rooted replay; any physical or interpretive reading of <>.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: In a three-event admission model where supply is the identity by stipulation: in the unrooted replay a mention of <> (or any token) is invisible to every function of the admitted state; in the rooted replay the first supply of <> is an admission precondition and only later supplies are inert; the model predicate HasCoproduct is independent of inscribing <> (the identification Real_0 = Difference join Structure is not modelled), and coproduct without inscription occurs only in the unrooted model; inertness is the model rule rather than a consequence of the spelling; verified exhaustively for all traces of length <= 5.
claim_boundary.next_test: Extend the finite model to the remaining three events of the six-operation alphabet (admit instance, admit rule, impose) with the refusal rules of admission.rs, and prove that supply stays inert and that no supply history forces a coproduct structure on the admitted state.

Findings the earlier pass missed: (1) supports and narrowest_claim say the first supply is an admission precondition and 'omitting it from an accepted history is refused'. The Lean anchor rooted_root_supply_is_precondition assumes the remaining history does not begin with a supply, and the native column root_omission_visible counts only histories whose second event is not the supply of <> (e.g. [s0,s0,...] minus its first s0 is still accepted; at L=2 the count is 7, not 8). The unqualified sentence is slightly too strong; it should say 'unless the next event is again the supply of <>'. (2) 'at lengths 1 to 5' for 1, 7, 49, 343, 2401: the records are cumulative over all traces of length <= L (1 + 6 + 42 + ...), not counts at length L; likewise 'refuses 7, 49, ...'. earlier_pass.notes: lean4/InertDiamond.lean (sha identical to p1 copy) recompiles exit 0; all theorems are propext/Quot.sound only. The result is honest that it is a consistency result for a DEFINITION, but the narrowest_claim still over-reads the model in three ways. (1) 'a mention of <> is invisible to every function of the admitted outcome' is true of the unrooted replay only. In replayRooted (the Lean model of the Rust gate: first event must be supply of <>), omitting the root supply changes the outcome from some to none (rooted_refuses_without_root), so the root mention is visible to refusal; supports says 'deleting every supply event changes no outcome or refusal', which is replay_filter_supply for replay, not for replayRooted. The Lean file has no theorem 'supplies after the root are inert under replayRooted', and mention_count_irrelevant only handles a leading block of supply-of-root events. No native column measures rooted supply deletion (supply_deletion_changes is computed on the unrooted model; mention_prefix_diff compares replay from INIT with replay from step(INIT, supply 0)=INIT, which is trivially identical because supply is the identity by definition). So those zero counts are consequences of the stipulated step rule rather than evidence; 'verified exhaustively' only confirms that the code implements the stipulated model, which the profile partly admits ('inertness is the model rule'). (2) 'coproduct identification' is not modelled: HasCoproduct is a stand-in predicate (an admitted datum classified diff AND an admitted datum classified struct under an arbitrary cls). The independence shown is independence of this predicate from supply/admission of <>; it is not independence of the identity <> = Real_0 = Difference join Structure. no_coproduct_of_single_token is near-trivial (one token has one class). (3) Of the two independence directions, 'coproduct without inscription' (coproduct_without_inscription) holds only in the UNROOTED model, which is explicitly not the rooted construction; in the rooted model every admissible history starts with the root supply, so inscription is necessary for any outcome and only 'inscription does not suffice' survives. The narrowest claim lists both directions without that qualification. Fidelity to Rust: genesis_construction.rs line 174 does gate index 0 on Supply("<>"), matching replayRooted; but the claim that admission::step is the identity on Supply and refuses arity 0 rests on admission.rs, which is not among the run inputs (only genesis_construction.rs, GenesisConstruction.lean, derivation_dag_witnesses.rs are), so the model-to-Rust correspondence is read, not mechanically checked. GenesisConstruction.lean itself treats supply-inertness as an explicit hypothesis (lines 115-147), consistent with the profile. Checker: re-implements the same stipulated model by a different algorithm (joint-state DP over string-encoded states, event set hard-coded to 3 tokens, coproduct = digits 1 and 2 present), so it verifies the counting of the model, not the model; it enforces record-level consistency conditions, all ints type-checked, case set compared sorted. 'for ANY classification' is Lean-only; native uses one fixed classification. Mutants: eight leaf-count edits, each a plausible misreading (supply moves state, inscription implies coproduct, coproduct requires inscription, root admission gives coproduct, mention count matters, inertness is spelling, rooted accepts everything, re-admission duplicates); the missing near miss is exactly the rooted one: 'the root supply is invisible to the rooted outcome' (rooted_ok vs refused would separate it), and 'supply of a non-root token as the first event is accepted' . next_test (extend to instance/rule/impose with admission.rs refusal rules) is this node's own unpaid obligation, distinct from does_not_support (which lists the three events as excluded, so next_test partly restates does_not_support, but adds the target theorem). DAG: status DEFINITION should stay; no theorem upgrades it.
